- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is rising, cap the increase at 2–3% above recent mean to avoid false optimism.  
- After a strong upward move in price (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast slope for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8) and forecast is trending, apply mean reversion bias: pull forecast toward 3-day moving average if deviation >2%.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >3% in 2+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 1–2% to avoid momentum bias.  
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) and price is rising, forecast should not exceed 1.5x recent 7-day high — avoid “over-leveraged” extrapolation.
